liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **House P.A. Music** (2 reviews): Listener enjoys what sounds like Elton John playing Honky Tonk Women over the house PA; The PA Honky Tonk Woman matches an Elton John recording dated 11-17-70, the following day, which the reviewer finds suspect [14][15]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review, 1 other source): Winwood, Capaldi and Wood joining in Not Fade Away would fit the 11/23 Traffic show better, says reviewer; Winwood adds vocal accompaniment through Not Fade Away > Goin' Down the Road > Not Fade Away, and sings the first verse [1][8]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Big Railroad Blues as a favorite of the set [7]

## The recordings

- **gd70-11-16.sbd.winters.17361.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 103 min; rated 3.79/5 by 28 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is excellent; Bobby sits far forward in the left channel, with Jerry and guests further back, mostly right; Disc 1 track 3 has analog distortion and channel dropouts, possibly from a loose plug on the master reel-to-reel [1][7]
- **gd1970-11-16.sbd.112987.flac**: soundboard; 12 songs; 80 min; rated 0.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1970-11-16.135717.aud.petlock.flac16**: audience recording; 1 songs; 10 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [3]

## Around the show

- That second-set tape circulated for years mislabeled as Anderson Theater, NYC, 11/23/70 [5]
- Reviewer thinks the date is really 11/23/70, since Winwood, Capaldi, Wood and Scarlett play these same songs then [6]
- Reviewer believes Deadbase has the date wrong for this tape [7]
- Concert was formerly thought to be 11/23/70 at the Anderson Theater; fresh research points to Fillmore East instead [9]
- A Fillmore East attendee recalls a Dead show simulcast on a New York radio station, lasting hours with everyone standing [11]
- Attendee says the Fillmore East show was announced under 48 hours ahead, at the late Zappa show that weekend [13]
- It was billed as the Airplane and the Dead, and was this reviewer's first Grateful Dead experience [13]
- Steve Winwood plays Pigpen's Hammond organ on Hard to Handle, Big Railroad Blues and Not Fade Away [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-11-16.sbd.winters.17361.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bill Gadsden and D. Winters; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Set 2 tape is believed to be from this night, mastered by the crew behind other surreptitious soundboards from the venue; A popular Traffic tape dated 11/23/70 at Anderson Theater, with Bill Graham introducing, is said to come from Bear's rig; The tape has been shrouded in mystery since it first entered circulation in 1973 [5][8][9]
- **gd1970-11-16.sbd.112987.flac**: source: SBD > RR > ? > ? > Cassette; Transfer Info: Nak MR2 Deck > Cassette > WAV >Soundforge > FLAC [2]. Also: A 2004 update says set 2 may be the tape long labeled Andersen Theater 11/23/70 [2]
- **gd1970-11-16.135717.aud.petlock.flac16**: taped by Rich Petlock; source: Partial; [3]. Also: A 2004 update says set 2 may be the tape long labeled Andersen Theater 11/23/70 [3]
